turns.query: The sheet that came with our pH probe says it is about due for a recalibration, but it never says how to do one. What do I actually dunk it in, and how many different solutions do I need?

relevant.evidence:
Standard USGS procedure for
calibration requires a two- or three-point calibration.
relevant.locator: Section 4.1.1 steps 6-10 — "Begin calibration procedures" and the pour-swirl-discard rinse sequence

relevant.evidence:
Use at least two pH buffer solutions with documented,
NIST-traceable pH values that bracket the sample pH
for accurate calibration of the pH instrument system.
relevant.locator: Section 4.0 calibration guidelines and section 4.1 Calibration Procedure — "Use at least two pH buffer solutions with documented, NIST-traceable pH values"

relevant.evidence:
A calibration curve is created by measurement of two or
more standard pH buffers that bracket the pH of the water
being measured.
relevant.locator: Section 3.3 long-term storage and section 4.0 Calibration of the pH Instrument System — "A calibration curve is created by measurement of two or more standard pH buffers"

relevant.evidence:
Most pH meters recognize
the e.m.f. range of certain pH buffers (commonly pH 1.68,
4.01, 7.00, and 10.01 buffers) and are able to automatically
compensate for temperature during calibration.
relevant.locator: Section 2.3 Standard pH Buffer Solutions — "Measurements of pH are only as accurate as the buffers"
Section 2.3 buffer precautions and Table 6.4–3 — "Values of pH from 0 to 90 degrees Celsius"

relevant.evidence:
If pH values are expected to be between 7 and 8,
then the standard pH-7 and pH-10.01 buffers (at a
minimum) should be selected.
relevant.locator: Section 4.0 Calibration of the pH Instrument System — "A properly working pH system has—"

relevant.evidence: brating a pH meter and electrode with buffers that are within±10 °C of the sample temperature is recommended.
relevant.locator: Section 4.0 temperature guidance and general calibration guidelines — "Calibrating a pH meter and electrode with buffers that are within ±10 °C"
